summary.headline: Seshaasai Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.1% YoY to INR 377 crore, but gross margin fell to 41.7% on war-linked input costs.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 377 crore, up 21.1% YoY but down 6.9% QoQ against a seasonally strong Q4. Cost of materials consumed rose to 58.34% (about 411 bps above the FY26 average), compressing gross margin to 41.7% from 44.5% a year earlier. EBITDA grew to INR 94 crore at a 25.1% margin (up 135 bps YoY), and PAT rose 63.8% YoY to INR 60 crore at a 16% margin. Management reiterated an 8-12% medium-term revenue growth target and guided to a stronger H2 on mix and operating leverage, without giving a numeric margin guide.

financial_highlights.change: about 411 bps above FY26 average of 54.23%

segments.name: Payment solutions
segments.commentary: 42% of Q1 revenue, growing about 5% YoY; premium metal cards cited as the main margin-accretive growth driver, with early export traction in Europe and Africa.

segments.name: Communication and fulfillment
segments.commentary: 40% of Q1 revenue, growing 13% YoY; management guides this segment to be roughly flat over the coming years, and it has the slightly lower EBITDA margin.

segments.name: IoT solutions
segments.commentary: 18% of Q1 revenue, growing 145% YoY; management expects about 45% growth in FY27 and 35-40% in FY28, with IoT at 15-18% of FY27 revenue.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue growth target of 8-12%; management said it expects about 8-12% YoY revenue growth for FY27.
No numeric gross margin or EBITDA guidance; management will give drivers (operating leverage, product mix, input costs) rather than figures.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, driven by seasonal BFSI demand, steady communication and fulfillment, and IoT growth.
Capex planned at INR 140-160 crore per year, maintained for FY27.
Payment solutions internal plan of about 12% CAGR; IoT 35-40% growth in FY28.
Bengaluru metal card facility expected operational by end of calendar 2026, subject to regulatory approvals; meaningful revenue expected from FY28, with possible small contribution in FY27.
capex_capacity: Overall capacity utilisation typically 65-70%, peaking at 85-90% during renewal cycles and month-end loads.
Greenfield metal card facility in Bengaluru described as almost ready; certification and compliance expected to start by Q4, with operations before end of calendar 2026.
Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities still under construction.
SIM card business capacity utilisation about 40% in Q1.
IPO proceeds: INR 24.4 crore deployed in Q1 (capex INR 6.7 crore, GCP INR 13.7 crore, issue expenses INR 3.9 crore).
demand_pricing: Two multi-year PSU bank tenders won in Q1, about INR 73 crore revenue over the tenure.
Top 10 customers about 56% of revenue; more than 95% from existing clients.
Input cost pressure attributed to the war: management said 40-45% of the impact is currency and the rest is commodity, logistics and freight.
Working with customers on price revisions to protect margins.
Chip prices broadly flat in Q1 procurement; marginal INR-neutral improvement offset by USD appreciation; company built chip inventory, and supplier lead times have lengthened.
Insurance client count fell (life 13 to 10, general 9 to 7) but management said the churned clients were near-zero business and no business was lost to re-tender.
Telecom SIM work with a large (third-largest) operator: about 20% of its pre- and post-paid SIM requirement, targeting 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: How should we look at full-year revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 8-12% revenue growth for FY27 and declined to give EBITDA or PAT figures, promising quarterly disclosure of margin drivers instead.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin drop is operating leverage versus pricing and rupee, and can costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed 40-45% of the input cost impact to currency and the rest to war-driven commodity, logistics and freight costs; operating leverage should improve margins quarter on quarter if conditions do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical utilisation is 65-70%, peaking at 85-90%; capex stays at INR 140-160 crore per year and the Bengaluru metal card facility should be operational before end-2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for IoT, cards and communication?
qa_highlights.answer: IoT to grow about 45% in FY27 and 35-40% in FY28; communication and fulfilment flat; payment solutions around 10-12% CAGR, with IoT contributing 15-18% of revenue by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of UPI and MDR on card business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UPI's impact on card issuance has already played out, that UPI adoption is near saturation, and that volume forecasts factor in UPI.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Bengaluru facility contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hoping for some contribution this year, with meaningful contribution from FY28 onwards, but declined to quantify.

risks_watch: Gross margin trajectory: COMC was 58.34% in Q1 vs 54.23% FY26 average; H2 recovery depends on operating leverage and product mix.
Input cost and currency: USD-denominated chip pricing; management is watching for upward price revisions and longer supplier lead times.
Communication and fulfilment is guided flat, so growth relies on IoT and payment solutions.
Payment solutions grew only about 5% YoY in Q1; the UPI and MDR debate could affect card volumes.
Bengaluru and Nagpur facility approvals and timelines.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 56% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the H2 recovery, but deliberately non-committal on margins, repeatedly declining numeric guidance and attributing pressure to war-related and currency factors outside its control.
key_quotes: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue.
